display.title: Erev Pesach in Yiddish: Resting, Seder Korban Pesach and Helping at Home
display.summary_short: A Yiddish talk for children on the rest of Erev Pesach: resting before the Seder, saying Seder Korban Pesach after Minchah, helping at home and what not to eat.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish to children, this talk continues the Erev Pesach preparations after the chametz is burned. Children help finish the preparations at home and then nap, so they will have strength at the Seder to ask the Four Questions, eat the matzah, drink the wine and the afikoman, and go to the door for Eliyahu HaNavi. After waking, they dress in Yom Tov clothes. In the days of the Beis HaMikdash the Korban Pesach was brought after the afternoon Tamid; today we daven Minchah and then say Seder Korban Pesach, and think about the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash and pray for it to be rebuilt. Helping one's parents on Erev Pesach, watching the baby or peeling apples and cracking nuts for the charoses, is a great mitzvah. Children must wash their hands well before touching anything in the Pesach kitchen. On Erev Pesach we do not eat matzah, so that we will eat it with appetite at the Seder, nor fruits and nuts that go into the charoses. Then Mother lights candles and everyone goes to shul.
display.lesson: Helping your parents prepare for Pesach is a great mitzvah, and we prepare ourselves so we can do the Seder's mitzvos with strength and appetite.
